summary: Tomoyuki Uno is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who taught Shindo Kusumoto. He held posts as a special researcher at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 1998) and assistant professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2000–2006).

Tomy Augustine is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned a master's at the University of Madras studying under C. S. Sundaram, and a PhD from Banaras Hindu University under Munni K. Agrawal. He held a post at Salesian College (attested 2008).

Toni Huber is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of Canterbury in 1993 under Paul Harrison and William Sax. He held professorships at Victoria University of Wellington (attested 2000) and Humboldt University of Berlin (attested 2006–2008).

Tony K. Stewart is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Western Kentucky University (~1972–1976). He taught in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at North Carolina State University (~1986–2011) and held a post at Vanderbilt University (~2011).

Torkel Brekke studied at the University of Oslo (MPhil ~1991–1995) and the University of Oxford (PhD 1996–1999 under Richard Gombrich). Working in religious studies, Indology, and history, he held posts at PRIO, Oslo Metropolitan University, and MF Norwegian School of Theology.

Toru Funayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology who studied at Kyoto University and under Ernst Steinkellner. He served as an associate professor at Kyushu University (attested 1999–2003) and as a professor at Kyoto University (attested 1995–2019).

Toru Haneda (1882–1955) was a scholar of Central Asian history and sinology educated at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He became a professor, dean, and library director at Kyoto University, and directed the Tōhō Bunka Kenkyūjo (~1931–1948).

Toru Kumeji specializes in Buddhist studies and computational fields. He has held positions at the Institute of Humanities Informatics and as a senior researcher at the Institute of Digital Humanities (attested 2015).

Toru Sagara (1921–2000) was a scholar of philosophy and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1943–1946) under Tetsuro Watsuji. He held academic posts at Ibaraki University (~1952–1968), the University of Tokyo (~1968–1982), and Kyoritsu Women's University (~1982–1997).

Toru Takahashi (1878–1967) studied at the University of Tokyo (1898–1902). A specialist in sinology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he served as a professor at Keijo Imperial University (1926–1940), Fukuoka University (1949), and Tenri University (1950–1964).

Toru Tomabechi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and computational fields. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Lausanne, later serving as an assistant at Lausanne (~1995–2000) and senior researcher at the Institute of Humanities Informatics (attested 2016–2018).
Toshiaki Yamada is a scholar in sinology and religious studies. He studied at Toyo University from ~1966 to 1970 and later held a post there from ~1982 to 2018.

Toshifumi Goto is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned his PhD at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg in 1982. He served as a professor at Osaka University and Tohoku University (attested 2003–2012).
Toshihide Unebe is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Issai Funahashi. He held an appointment as a professor at Doho University (attested 1991).

Toshihiko Izutsu (1914–1993) studied at Keio University, where he taught linguistics and Islamic philosophy (1954–1981). He also held posts at McGill University (1961, 1969–1975) and the Iranian Institute of Philosophy (1975–1979), working in philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies.

Toshihiko Kimura is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tohoku University (~1959–1963). He served as an assistant professor at Tokai Gakuin University (~1980) and professor emeritus at Shitennoji University (~2011).
Toshihiro Nakao is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Shuchiin University as an assistant professor (attested 1963) and as a professor (attested 1976).
Toshihiro Wada is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under V. N. Jha in 1981. He held an academic post, including as an assistant professor, at Nagoya University from ~1989 to 2019.

Toshiichi Endo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed undergraduate studies at the University of Kelaniya and earned a doctorate at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies in 1995 under Mahinda Palihawadana and W. S. Karunatillake.

Toshikazu Watanabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as a researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2011–2015) and became a professor at Kokugakuin University in 2018.
